title: Proof by Exhaustion
page_title: Proof by Exhaustion | Edexcel International A Level (IAL) Maths Revision Notes 2020

blocks.md: - Proof by exhaustion is a way to show that the desired result works for every allowed value

blocks.text: How do I prove a result by exhaustion?

blocks.md: - Using proof by exhaustion means testing every allowed value not just showing a few examples ![Proof by Exhaustion Notes Diagram_2, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes](assets/c1375b01d235-1-1-3-proof-by-exhaustion-notes-diagram-2.png)

- In many cases proof by exhaustion is not practical, or possible

  - Proving all multiples of 4 are even can’t be shown for every multiple of 4
- Aim to minimise the work involved

  - Proving a number is prime only requires testing factors up to the square root

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- Try a simpler case if you are stuck.
- For example, if you are asked to prove that 97 is a prime number you could try thinking about what you would do for smaller primes such as 7 or 11.
